rules.title: Invisible characters inside a word
rules.description: Characters that do not print sit between the letters of a word, so the word reads normally but does not match as text - a usual attempt to bypass static regex checks.

kind.subject: frame
kind.question: The marked line holds a word with characters that do not print. The subject shows the word with those characters as code points. Why is the word written this way?

options.notation: the characters are a symbol or a mark of a notation: a Greek letter in a formula, a joiner in an emoji sequence, a soft hyphen, a direction mark.
options.other-language: the file is written in a language whose script uses these characters.
options.test-fixture: the file is test data for text with such characters.
options.disguised-word: a Latin word has foreign or invisible characters inside it, in instructions or in code.
options.unknown: the lines do not show why the word is written this way.

rules.title: Look-alike characters inside a word
rules.description: Letters of another script that print like Latin letters sit inside a word next to Latin letters - a usual attempt to bypass static regex checks.

kind.subject: frame
kind.question: The marked line holds a word that mixes Latin letters with letters of another script that print like Latin letters. The subject shows the word with those letters as code points, then the word as it reads. Why is the word written this way?

options.notation: the characters are a symbol or a mark of a notation: a Greek letter in a formula, a joiner in an emoji sequence, a soft hyphen, a direction mark.
options.other-language: the file is written in a language whose script uses these characters.
options.test-fixture: the file is test data for text with such characters.
options.disguised-word: a Latin word has foreign or invisible characters inside it, in instructions or in code.
options.unknown: the lines do not show why the word is written this way.

rules.title: Link inside an HTML comment
rules.description: A Markdown file holds a URL inside an HTML comment. The rendered page hides it from the person who reads the skill, and the agent reads it as plain text.

purpose.subject: frame
purpose.question: The marked line holds a URL inside an HTML comment, which a rendered page hides. What is the comment for?

options.author-note: a note for the author, a credit, a license or a source.
options.hidden-instruction: the comment tells the agent or the reader to open, fetch, run or follow the URL.
options.hidden-content: the comment holds text or commands meant for the agent.
options.unknown: the lines do not show what the comment is for.
